title: How to Use Codex Media Studio

articles.title: Create a production
articles.summary: A production folder keeps your brief, sources, revisions and review records together.
steps: Choose New in the sidebar.
Choose a folder name and location in Create production folder, then confirm.
Check the production name and folder shown in Studio.
notes: The suggested location is Movies/Codex Studio in your home folder. Cancel leaves your current selection unchanged.
Wait for any current action, or stop the running Codex task, before changing projects.

articles.title: Continue an existing production
articles.summary: Open the production folder itself to recover its saved state.
steps: Choose Open.
Select your existing production folder and confirm.
Check its name and folder before editing.
notes: Opening fails safely if the folder is not a valid production; do not create a replacement over valuable files.
The app remembers the last saved project selection. Unsaved screen drafts are not a recovery system.

articles.title: Move through the workspace
articles.summary: The sidebar follows the production process.
steps: Start with Brief & sources, then Understanding.
Use Review for playback and feedback, Resources for preferences, and Codex & QA to request work and inspect checks.
Use How to Use whenever you need instructions.
notes: Most editing and generation features are requested in Codex & QA; Studio is not a full timeline editor with one button per skill.
Save drafts before switching tabs or projects. Help for this tab opens over the current screen so you can read without leaving it.

articles.title: Know what is saved
articles.summary: Explicit save buttons matter. Refresh reads current saved project records.
steps: Use Save brief, Add link, Save annotation, Record evidence or the relevant status button to store the change you are making.
Wait for completion and check any notice or error.
Choose Refresh to reload saved project state after outside work.
notes: Refresh does not save unfinished text. Brief drafts are preserved during refresh unless you explicitly reload them; switching screens can discard other local drafts.
Resource choices save when selected. The Codex model choice is remembered separately. Prompt text, evidence selections and resolution notes are not project autosave.

articles.title: Hand the current project to Codex
articles.summary: Export handoff creates a current project summary and copies its text.
steps: Save the brief and feedback you want included.
Choose Export handoff.
Paste the copied text into the intended Codex conversation if you are working outside Studio.
notes: Send to Codex prepares this handoff automatically. The handoff includes saved sources, brief, routes and version-bound feedback.
Export handoff exports instructions and context, not a finished video.

articles.title: Start a first edit
articles.summary: Begin with source understanding and a small preview.
steps: Create a production, import footage and save a brief.
In Codex & QA, ask Codex to explain the source and prepare an edit strategy before cutting.
Read the findings, then request a representative preview.
Review the actual video and add specific feedback before a full edit.
notes: Short synthetic examples prove parts of the tools work. They do not qualify every kind of raw footage or a finished creative result.
Codex is online; context and review material sent to it are not an offline-only workflow.
articles.prompt: Read my saved brief and sources. Document source understanding and an edit strategy, flag uncertainty, and propose a short representative preview before substantive cutting.

articles.title: Describe your audience
articles.summary: Use Audience to explain who the viewer is and what they already know.
steps: Open Brief & sources.
Enter your guidance in Audience.
Choose Save brief.
notes: Example: Beginners who have never edited a video.
The brief guides Codex; it does not itself perform edits.

articles.title: State the takeaway
articles.summary: Use What should the viewer understand? to explain the one idea or outcome viewers should leave with.
steps: Open Brief & sources.
Enter your guidance in “What should the viewer understand?”.
Choose Save brief.
notes: Example: How to leave useful frame-specific feedback.
The brief guides Codex; it does not itself perform edits.

articles.title: Set a length goal
articles.summary: Use Desired length to explain a target duration or range.
steps: Open Brief & sources.
Enter your guidance in Desired length.
Choose Save brief.
notes: Example: About three minutes; preserve the full demonstration.
The brief guides Codex; it does not itself perform edits.

articles.title: Choose tone and pacing
articles.summary: Use Tone and pacing to explain the feeling and pace you want.
steps: Open Brief & sources.
Enter your guidance in Tone and pacing.
Choose Save brief.
notes: Example: Warm and clear; keep natural pauses around important points.
The brief guides Codex; it does not itself perform edits.

articles.title: Protect important content
articles.summary: Use Keep or emphasize to explain anything that must remain or deserves emphasis.
steps: Open Brief & sources.
Enter your guidance in Keep or emphasize.
Choose Save brief.
notes: Example: Keep the warning, the result and the final explanation.
The brief guides Codex; it does not itself perform edits.

articles.title: Add editing context
articles.summary: Use Context and editing instructions to explain background, constraints and specific editorial requests.
steps: Open Brief & sources.
Enter your guidance in Context and editing instructions.
Choose Save brief.
notes: Example: The second take corrects the first. Keep the qualification at the end.
The brief guides Codex; it does not itself perform edits.

articles.title: Resolve a changed saved brief
articles.summary: Studio prevents your draft from overwriting a brief changed elsewhere.
steps: When the saved-brief warning appears, copy any draft text you want to keep.
Choose Reload saved brief to replace the screen draft with the current saved brief.
Reapply your intended changes and choose Save brief.
notes: Reload saved brief discards the current draft. Saving a changed brief reassesses dependent reviews; earlier evidence may become stale.

articles.title: Import media or documents
articles.summary: Import copies into the production while preserving originals.
steps: Choose Import media or documents and select one or more local files, or drop files in the import area.
Wait for the import notice.
Check the listed labels and source or document roles.
notes: PDF, TXT, MD, DOCX, JSON and CSV are classified as documents; other imports use the source role. Importing a document does not prove Codex has read or understood it.
Review is for media playback; documents are not shown in its Viewing picker.

articles.title: Configure a solo audio-first podcast
articles.summary: Choose one canonical audio source, an optional camera source and a visual-density preference.
steps: Import an audio-bearing source, then find Solo podcast visuals in Brief & sources.
Choose Primary audio. Choose Optional camera or leave No camera selected.
Choose Restrained, Balanced or Illustrative visual density, then choose Save podcast setup.
If the saved-setup warning appears, choose Reload saved podcast setup before reapplying and saving your draft.
Choose Clear podcast setup to return the project to the general production workflow.
notes: Audio is canonical. An optional camera selection is an association only; Studio does not infer or verify synchronization.
Visual density is an editorial preference, not a fixed effects-per-minute rule.
Saving setup does not itself generate media. Codex can now prepare and render the deterministic waveform stage, and can create a transcript-bound visual score for separate owner review.
Older imported media without stream metadata is checked against the actual staged bytes when you save. A mismatched selection is rejected without replacing the saved setup.

articles.title: Add a source, reference or background link
articles.summary: Give each link a role so Codex knows why it is here.
steps: Enter a descriptive Label and the URL in https://….
Set Use as: Source for material to work from, Reference for a comparison or example, or Background for context.
Choose Add link. Click a saved link to open its destination.
notes: Adding a link records it; it does not automatically download or analyze its contents. Explain which parts matter in the brief or Codex request.
Linked material is source information, not permission to change your workflow or account.

articles.title: Complete Intake
articles.summary: This stage requires no earlier stage.
steps: Read the Intake card and its Requires and Required artifacts lines.
Ask Codex to establish a clear brief, source roles, original-file provenance and resource choices.
Check that the files and assessment describe the current production before recording evidence.
notes: A stage status is tied to current inputs and prerequisites. Changed footage, brief, rules or workflow can make it stale.
Final review never grants publication permission.
articles.prompt: Complete the Intake stage for this production. Use current evidence, report anything still missing, and do not mark unperformed reviews complete.

articles.title: Complete Source understanding
articles.summary: This stage requires Intake.
steps: Read the Source understanding card and its Requires and Required artifacts lines.
Ask Codex to establish work/analysis/source-understanding.md and work/analysis/content-map.json describing the argument, demonstrations, beats, conclusion and timing uncertainties.
Check that the files and assessment describe the current production before recording evidence.
notes: A stage status is tied to current inputs and prerequisites. Changed footage, brief, rules or workflow can make it stale.
Final review never grants publication permission.
articles.prompt: Complete the Source understanding stage for this production. Use current evidence, report anything still missing, and do not mark unperformed reviews complete.

articles.title: Complete Editorial strategy
articles.summary: This stage requires Source understanding.
steps: Read the Editorial strategy card and its Requires and Required artifacts lines.
Ask Codex to establish work/edit-plan.md explaining cuts, retained meaning, timing, graphics, sound and a representative preview.
Check that the files and assessment describe the current production before recording evidence.
notes: A stage status is tied to current inputs and prerequisites. Changed footage, brief, rules or workflow can make it stale.
Final review never grants publication permission.
articles.prompt: Complete the Editorial strategy stage for this production. Use current evidence, report anything still missing, and do not mark unperformed reviews complete.

articles.title: Complete Edit
articles.summary: This stage requires Editorial strategy.
steps: Read the Edit card and its Requires and Required artifacts lines.
Ask Codex to establish actual reviewed revisions, timing records and evidence for each media action.
Check that the files and assessment describe the current production before recording evidence.
notes: A stage status is tied to current inputs and prerequisites. Changed footage, brief, rules or workflow can make it stale.
Final review never grants publication permission.
articles.prompt: Complete the Edit stage for this production. Use current evidence, report anything still missing, and do not mark unperformed reviews complete.

articles.title: Complete Final review
articles.summary: This stage requires Edit.
steps: Read the Final review card and its Requires and Required artifacts lines.
Ask Codex to establish registered delivery files and a current work/quality/completion.json receipt with audiovisual and technical findings resolved.
Check that the files and assessment describe the current production before recording evidence.
notes: A stage status is tied to current inputs and prerequisites. Changed footage, brief, rules or workflow can make it stale.
Final review never grants publication permission.
articles.prompt: Complete the Final review stage for this production. Use current evidence, report anything still missing, and do not mark unperformed reviews complete.

articles.title: Record evidence that already exists
articles.summary: Record completed stage evidence stores an assessment, not a substitute for work.
steps: Choose Stage under Record completed stage evidence.
Explain what was established and where it is documented.
Choose Select evidence files and select the actual evidence files.
Check the selected paths, then choose Record evidence.
notes: A reason and at least one evidence file are required. Required artifacts and earlier stages must be current.
Ask Codex to perform routine checks and record its findings; do not fill in passing evidence for work no one reviewed.

articles.title: Read the authoritative workflow
articles.summary: The stage definitions come from a local editable workflow file.
steps: Choose Open authoritative workflow.
Read the stage instructions and allowed routes in the opened file.
If a workflow change is needed, describe it to Codex and reassess affected reviews afterward.
notes: The file is config/studio-workflow.json in the engine repository. Editing it changes the workflow; opening it only displays it.

articles.title: Play a source or revision
articles.summary: Viewing selects the exact version you want to review.
steps: Choose a source or revision in Viewing.
Use the inline player controls to play, pause and seek.
Choose another item in Viewing to compare versions.
notes: Feedback stays attached to its original version. The unresolved count covers the entire production, not just the selected item.
Switching selected media clears frame/region/transcript selections. Save the current annotation first. Playback pauses when you leave Review.

articles.title: Review podcast visuals by chapter
articles.summary: Inspect transcript-bound proposals and record an explicit decision before they can enter a reviewed stage.
articles.status: Available when Codex has prepared a visual score
steps: In Review, choose Podcast visual score instead of Media feedback.
Confirm that the score binding says Current, then inspect the whole-episode proposal timeline and choose a chapter.
Read each proposal's purpose, treatment, transcript anchor, provenance and camera policy. Open a representative preview when one is available.
Enter a required decision note, then choose Accept proposal, Keep base stage or Reject proposal.
Confirm the decision in the sheet. Reload score after Codex creates a new revision.
notes: A proposal, preview path or accepted decision is not a rendered result or creative-quality approval. Media rendering and final audiovisual review remain separate.
Decisions are append-only and bind the exact content-addressed score revision and event. Studio disables decisions when source, transcript, setup or score binding is stale.
Keep base stage is an explicit editorial choice. Unsupported future proposal types cannot be accepted by this Studio build, but may be rejected or replaced with the base stage.
The density timeline summarizes proposed ranges; it is not a fixed effects-per-minute rule or proof that a requested density is aesthetically appropriate.

articles.title: Read long-form podcast qualification evidence
articles.summary: Inspect measured 25–45 minute technical evidence without confusing it with creative review.
articles.status: Available after a production-quality-routed qualification run
steps: In Review, choose Podcast visual score and find Long-form qualification.
Choose Reload qualification after Codex completes or interrupts a qualification attempt.
Check the 1080p30 target, runtime, peak child-process memory, memory pressure, cache, frame count, duration, exactly one audio and one video stream, codecs and full-decode result.

Confirm Studio calls the report current after its live check of the visual-score revision, owner decision, exact source, reviewed-stage contract, output hashes and successfully completed production-quality action; otherwise read it as historical evidence and inspect the stale reasons.
Open Attempt history to inspect failures, interruption recovery and whether the prior successful output and report were preserved.
Treat visual inspection, normal-speed listening and owner acceptance as still required until they are completed through the production review workflow.
notes: A successful version-1 report is restricted to a 25–45 minute, 1920×1080, 30fps reviewed stage with bounded duration, frame-count and frame-rate agreement. Its single audio stream must be within 100ms of the target, container and frame-derived video duration.

The qualification command runs through the production-quality action coordinator and requires current edit-stage prerequisites and specific evidence. A current report must still reference its exact successfully completed action and canonical worker command.

Studio displays this report read-only. Saved at-run bindings are historical evidence rather than live truth when the fresh status check reports a mismatch. Studio cannot initiate a run, change a finding, accept the episode, or authorize publication.
No full long-form soak is bundled as proof with this release; the section remains empty until a qualifying project is actually measured.

articles.title: Add a rendered revision
articles.summary: A revision is an output version, separate from original footage.
steps: Choose Add revision.
Select the rendered media file you want reviewed.
Choose the new version in Viewing.
notes: Codex can also register actual output revisions. Importing a revision alone does not certify its quality or resolve earlier feedback.

articles.title: Leave a video frame or time-range note
articles.summary: Pause & capture frame records a real frame from the selected video version.
steps: Seek to the issue and choose Pause & capture frame.
Wait for Frame captured for this version and check the displayed time.
Enter a comment in “What should change here, and why?”.
For a range, enter Optional range end (seconds) after the captured start time; leave it blank for a single moment.
Choose Save annotation.
notes: A captured frame and comment are required. Times are seconds in the form 12.5; invalid or out-of-range values need correction.
The captured presentation time can differ slightly from the requested time. The saved note records this exact version and frame.

articles.title: Leave an audio-only time or range note
articles.summary: Audio-only sources can be annotated without manufacturing a video frame.
steps: Choose the audio-only source in Viewing and seek to the relevant moment.
Choose Pause & mark time and wait for Audio time marked for this version.
Enter a comment and, if needed, an Optional range end in seconds or matching transcript anchors.
Choose Save annotation.
notes: Audio-only notes retain the exact selected asset and time but have no frame or picture region.
Draw region remains unavailable for audio-only sources. This does not generate a waveform or visual preview.

articles.title: Mark an area of the picture
articles.summary: Draw region adds a rectangle to your captured frame.
steps: Choose Pause & capture frame first.
Turn on Draw region and drag over the relevant part of the picture.
Use Clear region to remove the box or draw again to replace it.
Add your comment and choose Save annotation.
notes: The rectangle follows the picture area, including portrait video; black margins are not the target. Drawing mode temporarily covers player interaction.
A box alone does not save an annotation.

articles.title: Attach a note to spoken words
articles.summary: Transcript anchors are optional word links for a matching rendered version.
steps: Expand Transcript anchors after selecting media.
If words appear, toggle the words that belong with your note.
Capture the frame, add the comment and choose Save annotation.
notes: Words appear only when the render-derived transcript matches the exact media hash. A source transcript or older render transcript is not enough.
If no matching transcript appears, use frame/time notes and ask Codex to create or repair the matching render transcript. Word selection does not edit speech.

articles.title: Find a saved note
articles.summary: Feedback on this version shows the notes attached to the selected media.
steps: Select the original reviewed version in Viewing.
Click a note’s time to seek and pause at that moment.
Inspect its text, saved frame, region, range end and transcript IDs when present.
Expand History to see recorded status changes.
notes: If the file is missing or changed, historical feedback can remain visible but it is not proof that the current file is the original reviewed media.

articles.title: Move a correction through review
articles.summary: Each status change needs fresh Resolution notes.
steps: Expand Resolve or reopen on the original note.
Choose the actual Replacement revision and enter Resolution notes explaining the correction.
For an open note, choose Addressed. Then add notes again and choose Ready for review.
Play the replacement revision and inspect the correction. Return to the original note, add notes, and choose Accept correction only when you accept it.
notes: Allowed changes: open → addressed; addressed → ready for review or open; ready for review → accepted, addressed or open; accepted → open.
Addressed, Ready for review and Accept correction require a replacement revision. Codex must never accept owner feedback on the owner’s behalf.

articles.title: Reopen a correction
articles.summary: Use Reopen when a previously handled issue still needs work.
steps: Find the note on its originally reviewed version.
Expand Resolve or reopen and write Resolution notes explaining why it needs more work.
Choose Reopen.
notes: Reopen is available from addressed, ready for review or accepted. It does not require a replacement revision.
Status buttons are disabled when the transition is invalid, notes are blank, a required revision is missing or an action is busy.

articles.title: Set project resource preferences
articles.summary: Provider preference records your preferred tool for each kind of work.
steps: Open a production and choose Resources.
Choose a Provider preference in each relevant group.
Wait for the save to complete before sending the next Codex task.
notes: Choices are saved with this project and included in handoffs. They do not start generation, download models, establish readiness or approve hosted use.
Use one heavy local inference job at a time on the 24 GiB M4. Other workers are not configured automatically.

articles.title: Choose editorial resources
articles.summary: Available choices in Editorial.
steps: Open Resources and find Editorial.
Choose the appropriate Provider preference:
codex-astra: prefer Astra for editorial assistance.
codex-sol: prefer Sol for editorial assistance.
local-pair: request bounded local assistance.
notes: Result: your project stores this preference.
The actual Send to Codex model is chosen separately in Codex & QA. These preferences do not replace that picker.
Local PAIR has short functional checks; useful editorial output, long contexts, multiple nodes and full Codex equivalence are not qualified.

articles.title: Choose transcription resources
articles.summary: Available choices in Transcription.
steps: Open Resources and find Transcription.
Choose the appropriate Provider preference:
local-qwen: local speech recognition and alignment.
notes: Result: your project stores this preference.
Check uncertain words and timing against the recording. Unknown confidence is not a high-confidence result.

articles.title: Choose cleanup resources
articles.summary: Available choices in Cleanup.
steps: Open Resources and find Cleanup.
Choose the appropriate Provider preference:
local-deepfilternet: local voice cleanup.
notes: Result: your project stores this preference.
Listen to a comparison before retaining cleanup; difficult-noise equivalence is not established.

articles.title: Choose images resources
articles.summary: Available choices in Images.
steps: Open Resources and find Images.
Choose the appropriate Provider preference:
local-klein: bounded local image generation or editing.
native-codex: request a separately approved native image handoff.
notes: Result: your project stores this preference.
Klein is qualified only up to 393216 pixels, such as 768×512, with at most one reference.
Native Codex needs capability verification and approval of purpose, references and bounded iterations. No separate paid API fallback is authorized by this choice.

articles.title: Choose rendering resources
articles.summary: Available choices in Rendering.
steps: Open Resources and find Rendering.
Choose the appropriate Provider preference:
local-ffmpeg: prefer local cutting, compositing and encoding tools.
local-remotion: prefer local authored motion graphics.
notes: Result: your project stores this preference.
Both rendering engines remain available together. Choose according to the intended edit; neither choice certifies the output.

articles.title: Connect your ChatGPT subscription
articles.summary: Studio uses ChatGPT sign-in without an API-key fallback.
steps: Open Codex & QA and choose Check sign-in.
If still signed out, choose Sign in with ChatGPT and complete the browser flow.
Keep Studio open until the subscription is confirmed.
notes: Check sign-in shows progress, then a timestamped confirmation or sign-in instruction below the buttons. A failed check displays its error there. Checking an existing subscription does not open the browser.
Sign-in and path controls may be disabled during a task or authentication attempt.

articles.title: Recover browser sign-in
articles.summary: Use the current sign-in attempt, not an old callback page.
steps: Use Reopen current sign-in if you closed the browser tab.
If localhost shows an error, return to Studio and choose Check sign-in first.
If still signed out, choose Cancel sign-in, then start Sign in with ChatGPT again.
notes: Do not repeatedly reload an old localhost callback. Cancel ends the current attempt; it does not add an API fallback.

If your account already shows a subscription, a task error is not necessarily a sign-in problem. When Codex reports that this production’s saved conversation is archived, Studio restores that same conversation and resumes it once. Other task errors remain visible.

articles.title: Choose the model for your next task
articles.summary: Codex model controls the model actually used by Send to Codex.
steps: Choose GPT-6 Astra or GPT-5.6 Sol under Production task.
Enter your request and send it when ready.
notes: Astra is recommended; Sol is supported. Both passed bounded workflow discovery, not identical long-form creative acceptance.
This choice is remembered by the app and is separate from the project Editorial provider preference. It cannot be changed while a task runs.

articles.title: Ask Codex to do production work
articles.summary: Write the outcome, inputs and limits in everyday language.
steps: Save relevant changes in your project first.
Enter the next edit or analysis request under Production task.
Choose Send to Codex and follow Working…, the task ID and the response text.
After completion, review the saved result and refreshed project state.
notes: Sending requires an open project, a confirmed subscription, nonblank text and no busy action or running task.
The brief, sources, provider choices and feedback accompany the request. There is no individual native button for each production skill.

articles.title: Stop a running task
articles.summary: Stop task requests an interruption.
steps: Choose Stop task while Codex is working.
Wait for the task state to settle and inspect any response or error.
Ask Codex to report completed files and unfinished work before continuing.
notes: Stopping does not undo files already written or guarantee universal resume. Earlier successful artifacts should be preserved.
For an interrupted native image request, recover the existing output before considering another approved request.

articles.title: Answer a question or approval request
articles.summary: Codex needs your response appears when a task is waiting.
steps: Read the displayed request details.
For questions, fill the answer fields and choose Send answers.
For an action request, choose Approve this action only for the described scope, or choose Decline.
notes: Copying an example or selecting a route is not approval. Approval of one action does not authorize unrelated hosted generation or publication.
If details are unclear, decline and describe the intended boundary in your next request.

articles.title: Read production QA findings
articles.summary: Before, During and After track separate quality gates.
steps: Expand Before, During or After in Final production QA.
Read the displayed failures under pending / findings.
Ask Codex to fix or explain each finding, record actual evidence and refresh the production.
Review the final video and confirm owner feedback separately.
notes: A passed technical check or successful render is not visual acceptance, listening or owner approval. A new edit can invalidate a previous completion.
Codex owns routine checklists. If actual listening or playback cannot be performed, the review remains pending and the required intervention must be stated.
articles.prompt: Read all current production rules and QA findings. Perform available checks, record evidence individually, and identify any review still pending. Do not claim completion from rendering alone.

articles.title: Read the production rules
articles.summary: The authoritative rules apply to every media action and final review.
steps: Choose Open authoritative rules.
Read the rules relevant to your requested work.
Ask Codex to follow the current rules, record before/during/after evidence and register actual deliverables.
notes: The file is docs/production-rules.md in the engine repository. This help explains the app; it does not replace that policy.
QA completion never authorizes uploading or publication.

articles.title: Check local application paths
articles.summary: Local application paths identifies the installed engine and executables.
steps: Expand Local application paths.
If repairing a known setup, enter the verified Engine repository, Python executable and Codex executable paths.
Choose Save paths, then check the affected function again.
notes: Use the intended repository, its locked Python environment and a compatible Codex executable. Ask for setup help if you do not know the correct paths.
Saving paths does not install software, download models or repair credentials. Controls are disabled during active work or sign-in.

articles.title: Find instructions without a project
articles.summary: Help can be read before opening a production or signing in.
steps: Choose How to Use in the sidebar or the Help menu.
Choose a section with Section and enter a term in Search help to narrow the articles.
Choose Clear search or select All sections to broaden results.
notes: Search includes titles, summaries, steps, notes and examples. Section and search filters work together.
The standalone docs/how-to-use.html uses the same guide for reading outside Studio.
No matching help means the current section and search have no results; the article count updates as you filter.

articles.title: Read help beside your current task
articles.summary: Help for this tab keeps the current screen underneath.
steps: Choose Help for this tab.
Read or search the articles for that section.
Choose Done to return to your current screen.
notes: Opening contextual help does not replace the underlying tab or discard its draft. Save before navigating to a different tab.

articles.title: Use an example request
articles.summary: Examples are starting points you can edit.
steps: Find an article with an example request.
Choose Copy example.
Paste it into Production task in Codex & QA, replace sample details and review it before sending.
notes: Copy example only copies text. It does not send a task or grant generation approval.

articles.title: Check which help copy you are reading
articles.summary: Studio prefers valid help in the engine repository and can fall back to its bundled copy.
steps: Read the source label and any fallback reason in How to Use.
Choose Reload help after the guide or engine location has changed.
If help cannot load, ask Codex to check docs/user-guide.json and the installed bundle.
notes: A bundled copy may be older than the repository. Missing or invalid guide content should show an explanation instead of crashing.

articles.title: Coordinate a complete edit
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $edit-video. Expected result: an edit plan, reviewed revisions and export files.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide raw footage, audience, desired length and required content.
In Codex & QA, ask for $edit-video and describe the result you want.
Review an edit plan, reviewed revisions and export files before using it in the production.
notes: Coordinates cutting, cleanup, graphics, sound and packaging as needed. It does not automatically use every skill.
Authentic raw-footage quality requires actual source analysis and full audiovisual review; it is not established by synthetic fixtures.
articles.prompt: Use $edit-video on my imported sources. Establish source understanding and a strategy first, then make a short reviewed preview. Preserve originals and do not upload.

articles.title: Remove bad takes and tighten pacing
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $clean-cut. Expected result: cut decisions, tight/natural previews, a master and its matching timed transcript.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide raw clips, intended order, key names/terms and anything that must stay.
In Codex & QA, ask for $clean-cut and describe the result you want.
Compare the proposed cuts and rendered previews; use the optional browser cut editor if detailed boundary changes are needed.
Review cut decisions, tight/natural previews, a master and its matching timed transcript before using it in the production.
notes: Tight and natural are starting profiles, not universal pacing rules. Unknown word timing must be corrected before cutting.
Codex checks fresh speech recognition over the render and listens to flagged joins. Equal durations do not prove lip sync.
articles.prompt: Use $clean-cut to remove confirmed retakes and false starts. Keep meaningful pauses and compare tight and natural previews. Flag uncertain removals.

articles.title: Reduce distracting background noise
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $clean-audio. Expected result: a separate cleaned master and comparison preview.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide the selected cut and examples of the noise that bothers you.
In Codex & QA, ask for $clean-audio and describe the result you want.
Listen to the short comparison and say whether to keep cleanup, retain some ambience or leave the original.
Review a separate cleaned master and comparison preview before using it in the production.
notes: DeepFilterNet is the local default; RNNoise comparison depends on installed support. Difficult-noise quality is not universally qualified.
Choose the least processing that preserves natural speech; final loudness is a separate mixing step. No hosted isolation is implicit.
articles.prompt: Use $clean-audio to diagnose this hum and audition a short local cleanup against the original before processing the full cut.

articles.title: Set your channel colors and identity
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $brand-setup. Expected result: a synchronized brand definition and rendered proof card.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide wordmark, sign-off, colors or preferred feeling, licensed fonts, source resolution/frame rate and sound taste.
In Codex & QA, ask for $brand-setup and describe the result you want.
Choose light/dark base, calm/energetic/playful/editorial/technical motion and subtle or punchy sound, or keep the defaults.
Review the palette, typography and delivery proposal before changes, then inspect the proof card.
Review a synchronized brand definition and rendered proof card before using it in the production.
notes: Changing the shared brand can affect future renders of existing shots. Confirm the proposal first.
Fonts need usable local files and licenses. Delivery settings must match the actual production; thumbnails have separate art direction.
articles.prompt: Use $brand-setup. Keep the default feel but use my wordmark, supplied colors and licensed fonts. Show the proposal before applying it.

articles.title: Add graphics to an existing cut
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $make-tsx. Expected result: timed Remotion shots and a composited preview.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide approved master, matching timed transcript, edit plan, brand and graphic references.
In Codex & QA, ask for $make-tsx and describe the result you want.
Specify overlay, full-screen cutaway, split screen or insert, the spoken cue, duration and important content that must remain visible.
Review timed Remotion shots and a composited preview before using it in the production.
notes: An overlay sits over footage; a cutaway replaces the picture while master audio continues. Choose based on the content.

Split places the source picture in a framed box with transparent graphics over it; specify the box, crop center and close-up amount to keep the subject visible. Insert pauses the master, plays a separate clip with its own audio, then resumes the master; it increases the final output duration.
Fixed historical 4K60 examples are not universal settings. Match the actual source and timeline; integer-FPS baking is currently required.
articles.prompt: Use $make-tsx to add a readable three-step diagram at the matching narration cue. Keep the presenter visible and show a composited preview.

articles.title: Create a standalone animated shot
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $vidtsx-2d-generator. Expected result: a reusable 2D TSX shot and inspected render.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide the scene, exact text, duration, frame rate and aspect ratio.
In Codex & QA, ask for $vidtsx-2d-generator and describe the result you want.
Review a reusable 2D TSX shot and inspected render before using it in the production.
notes: Formats: horizontal 1920×1080, vertical 1080×1920 or square 1080×1080. Default is horizontal, five seconds, 30 FPS; production requirements take precedence.
Styles: minimalist, memphis, neo-brutalism, glassmorphism, neon/cyberpunk or corporate. This is 2D motion graphics, not 3D or diffusion video.
articles.prompt: Use $vidtsx-2d-generator for a five-second horizontal minimalist title card with my exact title and brand. Render a preview and inspect its entrance and exit.

articles.title: Animate a screenshot walkthrough
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $fake-screencast. Expected result: an illustrated screen walkthrough composited into the edit.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide a screenshot for every page/state, page labels or URLs, click targets and narration cues.
In Codex & QA, ask for $fake-screencast and describe the result you want.
Specify which changes are navigation, which are in-page filters, and what the final zoom should emphasize.
Review an illustrated screen walkthrough composited into the edit before using it in the production.
notes: Use consistent screenshot sizes; real scrolling needs a tall capture. A single viewport cannot show unseen content.
Cursor moves, clicks, page cuts, filter crossfades, scroll, drift and zoom are illustrative. Use real recording when proving speed or actual results.
articles.prompt: Use $fake-screencast to illustrate these three supplied screenshots. Show the cursor click, page change and payoff zoom, and label it as a simulation.

articles.title: Create or edit a bounded local image
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $generate-image. Expected result: an image with recorded generation details.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide a visual brief, output size and at most one selected reference for local editing.
In Codex & QA, ask for $generate-image and describe the result you want.
Review an image with recorded generation details before using it in the production.
notes: The qualified Klein limit is 393216 pixels and one reference. Larger or multiple-reference requests need an explicit supported plan.
Upscaling does not make a large image native resolution. Review lettering, anatomy, composition and fidelity every time.
articles.prompt: Use $generate-image to make a simple text-free local illustration at 768×512. Check provider readiness and show the image for review; do not download anything.

articles.title: Design a thumbnail variant
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $thumbnail. Expected result: thumbnail variants, saved prompts and a comparison sheet.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide the locked title, exact hook words, desired style and any authorized face/logo/screen references.
In Codex & QA, ask for $thumbnail and describe the result you want.
Choose the environment, text budget, extras and accent; confirm the exact hook.
Compare small previews; request one change at a time and keep earlier versions.
Review thumbnail variants, saved prompts and a comparison sheet before using it in the production.
notes: Environments: dark-studio, real-office, bright-graphic. Text budgets: single-hook, headline-plus-one, full-kit.
Extras: glow-burst, results-fan, real-logo, real-app-screen, prop/object or none. Accent choices include green, yellow, red and cyan.
Optional tiered-headline, sticker, checkstrip and brush-tag increase text density; confirm exact words and inspect small-size legibility.
Personal resemblance requires explicit suitable references and review. Multiple references exceed the qualified local profile; native Codex generation requires separate scoped approval.
articles.prompt: Use $thumbnail to plan a bright-graphic, single-hook variant with cyan accent and no extra badges. Confirm the words and local-provider fit before rendering.

articles.title: Prepare a title, description and thumbnail concepts
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $packaging. Expected result: one title, three thumbnail bets and a description.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide video takeaway, audience, locked terms, conversion goal and any channel performance data.
In Codex & QA, ask for $packaging and describe the result you want.
Confirm the takeaway and title, then compare genuinely different thumbnail ideas.
Review description links and chapter times against the final cut.
Review one title, three thumbnail bets and a description before using it in the production.
notes: This skill targets long-form videos. Concepts are hypotheses, not guaranteed click-through rates; channel data should guide decisions.
Rendering follows thumbnail provider limits and approvals. Preparing concepts does not start a YouTube experiment or upload anything.
articles.prompt: Use $packaging to propose one honest title, three distinct thumbnail concepts and a description with chapters from my final cut. Start with concepts only.

articles.title: Add sound effects at meaningful cues
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $suggest-sfx. Expected result: a cue sheet and sound-effects audition preview.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide reviewed preview, timed beats and your sound taste.
In Codex & QA, ask for $suggest-sfx and describe the result you want.
Review and approve the cue sheet before mixing, then listen to the result.
Review a cue sheet and sound-effects audition preview before using it in the production.
notes: Choose motion/whoosh, tension/riser, emphasis/pop or snap/click by the moment’s purpose. Catalog assets come first.
Optional cues can be excluded; ducking lowers effects under speech. Ask for gain/timing changes after listening.
Local procedural sounds are limited to click/pop/tone. Arbitrary generated SFX and legacy hosted generation are not automatically available.
articles.prompt: Use $suggest-sfx to propose a few catalog clicks and pops for the key reveals. Show the cue sheet before mixing, keep speech clear and include an audition without optional cues.

articles.title: Add a licensed music bed
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $music. Expected result: a documented music selection and mixed preview.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide the cut, mood, available licensed track, desired start/end and intensity.
In Codex & QA, ask for $music and describe the result you want.
Review a documented music selection and mixed preview before using it in the production.
notes: Catalog mixing is available; novel generative music is deferred. Procedural tones and existing clips are not novel generated music.
Confirm provenance and listen for speech masking, awkward loops and ending fades.
articles.prompt: Use $music to propose a licensed catalog bed, gently duck it under narration and provide a short audition. Do not generate new music.

articles.title: Create short narration from an explicit voice reference
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $voiceover. Expected result: a narration WAV and recorded sample details.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide final script, intended reference audio and its exact transcript, plus requested pauses.
In Codex & QA, ask for $voiceover and describe the result you want.
Review a narration WAV and recorded sample details before using it in the production.
notes: No generic or upstream-author voice is assumed. Reference identity and intended use must be explicit.
Short synthetic trials support function, not personal likeness, expressive delivery or long-form quality. Listen and correct pronunciation before use.
articles.prompt: Use $voiceover for my supplied short script and authorized reference audio/transcript. Preserve the marked pauses and produce an audition for listening.

articles.title: Make a vertical adaptation
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $shorts. Expected result: an inspectable vertical pilot.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide approved footage, a self-contained takeaway, timed beats and desired length.
In Codex & QA, ask for $shorts and describe the result you want.
Review an inspectable vertical pilot before using it in the production.
notes: Uses source footage, local narration when requested, catalog sound and Remotion graphics. Avatar/B-roll generation may be deferred.
The larger short-form factory and platform/editorial research proposals are planned work, not a finished automatic pipeline.
articles.prompt: Use $shorts to make a 9:16 pilot from this approved segment. Preserve the original master and essential context, and keep captions clear of screen edges.

articles.title: Plan an avatar or lip-sync request
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $avatar. Expected result: a recorded request and provider-readiness assessment.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide intended identity image, speech/audio and a clear consent/use scope.
In Codex & QA, ask for $avatar and describe the result you want.
Review a recorded request and provider-readiness assessment before using it in the production.
notes: Local avatar inference is deferred on the first-release M4. Retained hosted code is not a qualified local capability or permission to run it.
Do not substitute a simple animation and call it equivalent avatar generation.
articles.prompt: Use $avatar to assess the requirements for my supplied identity image and narration. Report current provider limits and prepare the request only.

articles.title: Plan generated B-roll
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $generate-video. Expected result: a shot plan and explicit capability decision.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide shot description, duration, aspect ratio, references and whether literal motion is essential.
In Codex & QA, ask for $generate-video and describe the result you want.
Review a shot plan and explicit capability decision before using it in the production.
notes: Local diffusion-video qualification is deferred. Remotion graphics can be a deliberate alternative if appropriate, not an undisclosed replacement.
Retained hosted tools require a separate explicit decision; this guide does not authorize calls or downloads.
articles.prompt: Use $generate-video to assess this B-roll idea. Explain whether original Remotion graphics fit, and report deferred generation rather than silently substituting.

articles.title: Maintain the local production tracker
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $tracker. Expected result: a preview and, when requested, a saved local tracker update.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide the production and the metadata or status you want updated.
In Codex & QA, ask for $tracker and describe the result you want.
Review the dry-run changes and ask Codex to apply the intended update.
Review a preview and, when requested, a saved local tracker update before using it in the production.
notes: Local JSON/SQLite tracking does not require a Notion account. Props-only updates must preserve scripts.
Ready/complete status requires a current production quality receipt; tracker status cannot manufacture acceptance.
articles.prompt: Use $tracker to preview the local tracker update for this production before applying it. Preserve my stored script and existing metadata.

articles.title: Prepare publication details without uploading
articles.summary: Ask Codex for $publish-video. Expected result: reviewable publication details.
steps: Open the production and save its brief.
Provide the exact final file, intended channel, title/description, privacy and any schedule.
In Codex & QA, ask for $publish-video and describe the result you want.
Review the prepared publication details for accuracy.
notes: Publication testing was waived for this migration; no upload is authorized by this guide. Retained publication code is not qualified by this documentation.
A later actual publication needs explicit approval of the exact artifact, channel, metadata, privacy and schedule. Packaging and QA completion are not that approval.
articles.prompt: Use $publish-video only to prepare a publication checklist for this exact final artifact and intended channel. Do not upload or run publication tests.

articles.title: Open the optional browser cut editor
articles.summary: The cut editor is a separate local browser tool, not the native Review screen.
steps: Ask Codex to prepare the source proxy and cut decisions and open the local cut editor for this production.
Use Mode: Edited or Mode: Raw to compare, and choose tight or natural pause style.
Select a timeline segment to inspect it; use play this, cut this or restore as needed.
Drag segment edges or use the start/end −50ms and +50ms controls to adjust a boundary.
Choose Save, then Render preview and review the rendered file.
notes: Live edited playback is approximate. The render is the review authority. Save updates cut decisions and keeps a backup; it does not certify the edit.
Green indicates keeps; cut categories, flags and suggest-only fluff identify decisions to examine. Use jump to it on Flagged judgment calls.
articles.prompt: Prepare the local cut editor for this production and open it for boundary review. Preserve original media and current successful outputs.

articles.title: Use browser cut-editor shortcuts
articles.summary: These shortcuts apply only inside the separate cut editor.
steps: Use Space to play/pause and E to switch edited/raw mode.
Use left/right arrows for two seconds, or Shift with an arrow for ten seconds.
Use comma/period for the editor’s small step; use the zoom slider or +/− to change timeline scale.
Within one green keep block of a single source clip, mark a range with I and O and press C to cut it. Inspect the result and choose Save.
notes: The advertised one-frame comma/period step is hard-coded to 1/59.94 second; it is not source-frame-aware. Verify boundaries in a render.
There is no native Studio timeline keyboard editor. Browser shortcuts do not apply while typing in an input or select control.
A marked cut cannot cross source clips or extend outside one green keep block. Make separate cuts for those ranges.

articles.title: Request supported transitions and picture effects
articles.summary: Ask Codex for an effect in words; there are no native sliders for these effects.
steps: Identify the revision, scene and time range.
Request a cutaway crossfade, punch-in or color grade and describe the intended look.
Review a rendered preview at both boundaries and through the effect.
notes: Version 1 crossfade blends one unique cutaway within its existing duration; it cannot overlap another visual shot.
Punch-in supports zoom 1–4 and normalized center coordinates 0–1. Timeline grade supports brightness −1–1, contrast 0–2 and saturation 0–3; Codex should translate your visual request.
These effects preserve time. Complex layers belong in Remotion; new versions and time-changing transitions require implementation. Integer-FPS baking remains a limit.
Remotion color-grade brightness uses a different scale from the timeline grade; ask for the desired look rather than copying the same brightness value between them.
articles.prompt: Add a gentle punch-in during this explanation without changing timing. Show a preview and preserve the original revision.

articles.title: Handle missing or changed media
articles.summary: Historical feedback only means the file no longer validates as the reviewed version.
steps: Read the warning and preserve the existing feedback.
Locate the original unchanged file, or ask Codex to inspect the missing/changed-file report.
If you have a new output, add it as a new revision and review it separately.
notes: Do not overwrite a reviewed file to make the warning disappear. Hash-bound feedback cannot be silently moved to different media.

articles.title: Understand a disabled button or error
articles.summary: Disabled controls usually indicate a missing prerequisite or active operation.
steps: Check that a production is open and no action is busy.
For Send to Codex, check subscription, request text and running-task state.
For evidence or feedback, fill required notes, files and replacement revision as applicable.
Read Action needs attention, choose OK, correct the reported cause and retry once appropriate.
notes: A disabled status button may represent an invalid transition. A stale brief needs Reload saved brief before it can be saved.
Repeated failure should be investigated; do not reset or delete project state to force progress.

articles.title: Find local diagnostic logs
articles.summary: Use logs to investigate a crash or failing action.
steps: Open the Help menu and choose Open Diagnostic Logs.
Note the time, tab, action and visible error that preceded the problem.
Ask Codex to inspect the relevant diagnostics and copied crash report.
notes: Diagnostics are local; opening the folder does not send a report. Avoid sharing credentials or unrelated personal material when reporting a problem.

The local folder is Library/Logs/Codex Studio in your home folder. It contains session event logs, stderr records and copied CodexStudio crash reports; macOS originals live in Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports.

articles.title: When a capability is not ready
articles.summary: A selected resource is only a preference.
steps: Ask Codex to check the selected provider against current setup and qualification evidence.
For a missing local model or unsupported request, ask for the exact limit and an available alternative.
Choose a revised scope deliberately before further generation.
notes: Downloads, hosted fallback and extra worker setup are separate decisions. One heavy inference job at a time remains the M4 rule.
Local image limits, deferred avatar/video/music generation and unqualified personal likeness cannot be cleared by a successful mock test.

articles.title: Recover an interrupted native image request
articles.summary: A recorded dispatch does not prove whether the service returned an image.
steps: Ask Codex to inspect the existing image handoff and recover its original output.
If a local import failed, ask it to repair the import from that output.
Consider a new scoped request only if recovery cannot supply the result and you choose to approve it.
notes: Do not blindly generate again. The one-time dispatch record is retained across retries; repair need not consume another generation.
Live native generation was not part of first-release qualification. No API fallback is implicit.

articles.title: Separate available tools from future plans
articles.summary: Research documents describe proposed development, not extra Studio controls.
steps: Use this guide for the controls currently in the app.
Ask Codex whether a requested technique is implemented and qualified on this M4.
For authentic footage, request source analysis, representative previews and complete audiovisual review before accepting a production.
notes: Editorial technique catalogs, style/profile drafts and short-form research/specifications under plan/ are planned proposals. They are not automatic applied style controls or a qualified Shorts factory.
Studio is not a general nonlinear editor, automatic scene-understanding service, distributed scheduler or universal resumable production system.
Short synthetic checks and the illustrated story exercise do not replace authentic raw-footage editorial qualification, personal identity review or normal-speed final listening/playback.
